[h1]UNPLAYABLE COMPONENT CRISIS: Version 7.0.0 "Conquest" completely broke the game.[/h1]
I am writing this review as a dedicated player who has invested significant time, effort, and hard-earned money into this game—even pushing all the way to securing the Number 1 Player rank on the leaderboards. Up until recently, I supported this project. However, the deployment of the Version 7.0.0 "Conquest" update has fundamentally broken the core loop of the game, rendering it completely unplayable and fundamentally broken from a technical standpoint.
If you are thinking about downloading this game or purchasing microtransactions, STAY AWAY until the developers fix their servers.


[h1]1. Structural Server & Client Instability[/h1]
Since the 7.0.0 patch dropped, the game is plagued by severe, constant client crashes straight to the desktop. The main game menus are structurally unstable, entirely failing to handle traffic or load asset files for the new Conquest game mode. Background WebSocket connection errors constantly drop, meaning even if you can stay logged in for more than five minutes, the game client completely desyncs from the actual developer servers.


[h1]2. Broken Progression & Leveling Deadlocks[/h1]
Because the game client fails to communicate reliably with the server databases, all forms of progression are completely frozen. Attempting to level up or transition into a new diversion results in infinite loading loops or immediate game crashes. Your time is completely disrespected here; you can grind out objectives only for the server to throw a "Loading - Disconnect" error, wiping away any immediate progress you just attempted to make.


[h1]3. Total Failure to Deliver Earned Rewards[/h1]
The most egregious issue is how the server desyncs handle leaderboard data and premium transactions. After putting in the effort to achieve the Number 1 Player spot, the broken state of the server infrastructure completely failed to distribute my ranking rewards. No rewards are triggering, milestones are locked, and the game is effectively withholding content that was earned. To make matters worse, premium items and packages purchased right before the patch are entirely trapped behind these technical blocks.


[h1]4. Zero Support for Consumer Issues[/h1]
When you run into these game-breaking issues, you are entirely on your own. Steam automated systems cannot directly refund third-party in-game consumable wallet transactions, meaning you are forced to deal with Pochemu LTD’s slow support ticketing system. The developers pushed an unvetted, critically unstable update out to live servers, locked players out of their content, and left the player base hanging without immediate emergency hotfixes.


[h1]Final Verdict:[/h1] Do not buy combat packs, do not buy mascots, and do not waste your time grinding ranks that the server will just delete or forget. A game cannot call itself functional when a single update introduces total progression deadlocks and constant desktop crashes. Avoid this until a massive stability overhaul is pushed.

Everlusting Life is a fantasy-themed auto-battler that combines strategic squad building, character collection, romance, and explicit adult content into a free-to-play RPG framework. Developed and published by Pochemu LTD, the game is clearly designed for a particular adult audience, but there is more beneath its provocative presentation than a simple collection of mature scenes. Its main attraction comes from developing a roster of distinctive heroines, arranging them into effective teams, improving their abilities, and gradually progressing through a magical adventure in which combat and relationships are closely connected.

The story places the protagonist in another world where the survival of a magical realm is threatened. At the center of the conflict are Eternitas, her Demigoddess daughters, and the Cosmic Seed, which becomes an important part of the plan to prevent catastrophe. The daughters have their own intentions rather than simply obeying what is expected of them, leaving the protagonist to locate them and establish relationships with them. It is deliberately exaggerated fantasy storytelling, mixing heroic responsibilities with romantic pursuits. The narrative is primarily a framework for introducing new characters and giving the player's growing collection a reason to participate in the larger adventure, but it nevertheless provides more context than simply moving from one battle or intimate encounter to another.

Combat follows an auto-chess approach, meaning preparation is considerably more important than rapid inputs during an encounter. Players assemble a squad, consider the strengths of individual characters, arrange a suitable lineup, and allow much of the actual fighting to unfold automatically. This creates an accessible strategy system that works particularly well for players who enjoy optimization. Finding useful combinations and developing an increasingly capable roster provides much of the satisfaction. However, the same automation can make battles feel passive. Players who prefer directly controlling attacks, movement, or abilities may find the moment-to-moment gameplay lacking involvement, especially after the underlying battle patterns become familiar.

Character collecting is consequently one of the game's strongest motivational systems. New heroines represent both additional personalities to discover and potential additions to a player's tactical lineup. This gives collection a practical purpose beyond unlocking attractive artwork. Experimenting with characters can change how a squad performs, while upgrades encourage continued investment in favorites. The combination of RPG progression and auto-battler mechanics produces a straightforward loop of collecting, strengthening, reorganizing, and testing teams. Competitive PvP provides another place to put developed squads to use, adding longevity for players interested in optimizing formations against something beyond routine encounters.

Romance and mature material are equally central to Everlusting Life. This is explicitly an adults-only experience featuring nudity and sexual situations rather than a conventional fantasy RPG that happens to contain occasional suggestive material. Relationships with the female cast are deliberately tied to the player's broader progression and serve as an important reward for continued interaction. Players specifically seeking an adult character-collection game will therefore find the title much more substantial than those expecting its erotic elements to remain secondary. Conversely, anyone primarily interested in fantasy strategy without explicit content is clearly outside the intended audience.

The visual presentation emphasizes colorful anime-inspired characters and fantasy imagery. Character designs are particularly important because collecting and interacting with heroines forms such a large part of the experience. There is enough variety among the cast to reinforce the feeling that the player is gradually assembling a substantial fantasy roster. Pochemu LTD also discloses the use of neural-network technology during pre-production to assist artists with rendering finer character details, while stating that the designs are planned and created by its artists and writers and that the game does not generate AI content live during gameplay.

The free-to-play structure is where the experience becomes more divisive. Everlusting Life contains regular in-game purchases as well as chance-based purchases, creating the familiar tension between natural progression and spending. Collecting and upgrading characters can be enjoyable when progress feels steady, but considerably less rewarding when resource restrictions or monetized shortcuts become too noticeable. This is especially significant in a game where acquiring and strengthening characters is the foundation of both combat and relationship progression. Players comfortable with long-term free-to-play progression will probably tolerate this structure more easily than those who prefer purchasing a game once and receiving an evenly paced progression system.

Repetition is another concern. Automatic battles are convenient for extended play sessions, yet convenience can eventually become monotony because players spend more time managing progression than actively participating in combat. Everlusting Life is strongest when new characters, upgrades, strategic combinations, story developments, and relationship rewards arrive frequently enough to maintain momentum. When progression slows, its underlying cycle becomes much more visible. The PvP component helps by introducing less predictable opposition, although competitive play also increases the importance of maintaining a capable roster.

Steam Deck compatibility is a positive aspect, with the game officially categorized as Playable rather than Verified. Its default controller configuration provides access to the game's functionality, and the default graphics settings perform well on the handheld. There are nevertheless some compromises. Certain prompts can display mouse, keyboard, or non-Steam Deck controller icons, some text may appear rather small on the Deck's screen, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. These issues prevent a completely seamless handheld experience, but they are relatively manageable. For a collection-focused auto-battler that does not depend on rapid precision controls, portable play is nevertheless a sensible fit.

Everlusting Life ultimately offers a surprisingly broad package within its very specific adult-oriented niche. Its mixture of fantasy storytelling, heroine collection, romance, squad development, auto-chess battles, progression systems, and PvP gives players several interconnected reasons to continue playing. The strategic component is accessible rather than exceptionally deep, and the automatic battles will not satisfy everyone, but constructing effective teams gives the gameplay enough purpose to support the character-driven content.

The main obstacle is its monetization model, which can diminish the satisfaction of progression and makes the experience more dependent on a player's tolerance for free-to-play mechanics. Even so, Everlusting Life has a recognizable identity and understands its target audience. Players interested in adult anime fantasy, character collecting, gradual roster development, and relatively relaxed strategic combat may find plenty to enjoy, particularly with the option of playing comfortably on Steam Deck despite a few interface inconveniences.

One of the more predatory examples of the "waifu auto-chess" genre. It feels less like a game and more like a storefront wearing a thin layer of strategy mechanics to get you in the door. Everything about Everlusting Life is built to sell you overpriced currency and character unlocks, not to actually entertain you.

The progression system is designed to frustrate on purpose. Early battles feel fine, almost promising, but the moment you hit the free-tier wall, everything grinds to a halt. Unit upgrades, squad slots, even basic resource gains all funnel you toward the cash shop. It's not balanced around skill or strategy, it's balanced around your willingness to spend.

You'll be hit constantly with currency bundles, character summon pulls, and "limited time" offers, and that's really the whole game underneath the surface. Pay to unlock characters, pay to progress, pay to stay competitive. If the developers wanted a paid game this badly, they should have just charged upfront instead of dressing up a mobile-style gacha grind as a free strategy title.

There's nothing here worth your time. It's a hollow shell built around a payment funnel, not a game. Skip it.
